historical_feature_boundary.findings: shift(1) strictly applied prior to rolling aggregations. No current or future targets leak into historical features. Operates exactly under the documented one-step-ahead assumption (T-1 target is available at T).

linear_regression_anomaly.findings: LinearRegression (raw, GroupB) achieved R2=0.9573. This is structurally plausible because building energy usage is highly autocorrelated (AR(1) process). A linear combination of lag_1 and rolling_mean_24 strongly predicts the current state. No implementation defect was found.

december_holdout.findings: December 2016 was strictly bypassed in the train_models loop. Test rows were only preprocessed and then dropped from memory.

model_stability.findings: Qualitative ordering is highly stable between 1% and 10%. Group B massively outperforms Group A. log1p models continue to exhibit extrapolation explosions without tuning (LinearRegression, log1p, Group B R2 = -49,291,116).

research_questions.RQ1: Raw targets strongly outperform log1p in this untuned configuration when evaluated on original energy scale. log1p models suffer from catastrophic exponentiation of extrapolation errors.
research_questions.RQ2: Historical features (Group B) provide overwhelming predictive power, pushing R2 from ~0.79 (exogenous only) to ~0.95. The problem is fundamentally autoregressive.
research_questions.RQ3: Yes, patterns are stable. Row counts scaled roughly 10x (Train: 1,609,317 vs 221,885), and model families retained their qualitative behavioral characteristics.
